# Protik Roychowdhury — protik.info

> VP Product at Intellect (regulated multi-tenant enterprise SaaS, 4M+ users, $20M+ ARR) | Three-time founder, one exit | Academic researcher | ICF-certified coach

## About

Protik Roychowdhury is VP Product at Intellect, a regulated, multi-tenant enterprise SaaS platform serving 4M+ users across APAC, ANZ, China, and Latam in the workforce health category. He leads a 20+ person product, design, content, localisation, and AI team. He drove enterprise revenue to $20M ARR by leading the pivot from consumer app to B2B2C care ecosystem, shipped GenAI features (triage, session prep, treatment plans), and co-authored 3 academic papers on AI in mental health.

Before Intellect, Protik was Principal PM for Growth, Engagement & Loyalty (GEL) at Grab ($3.8B+ revenue superapp), where he increased ARPU by 2% via personalisation and gamification, boosted onboarding success by 15pp, built engagement tools unlocking $2.5M in ad revenue, and delivered $4.5M in cost savings on the Driver Rentals product for 30K+ vehicles. He held product leadership roles at Ola (India's largest ride-hailing platform — reduced revenue leakage by INR 9.7M, improved driver earnings by 12%), Fabelio (Indonesia e-commerce — increased showroom conversions by 18pp, first senior product hire), and Exotel (India's leading cloud telephony platform).

Protik is a three-time founder: Croak.it! (voice-based social platform, 1M recordings, 200K downloads, acquired by Exotel), Bhalu.com (hyperlocal task marketplace — post odd jobs, anyone could fulfil them; 2009-2011, built in college), and Athlete Diaries / The Players' Diary (India's version of The Players' Tribune).

He is an IIT Kharagpur alumnus (B.Tech Hons, Metallurgical & Materials Engineering, GPA 8.19) and an ICF-certified career coach working with product managers, founders, and senior leaders. Also a Certified Mental Health First Aider (MHFA).

## Authority Pillars

Protik's expertise spans five core authority pillars:

1. **AI Product Strategy** — Shipping GenAI features in regulated industries, AI personalisation at scale, human-AI balance
2. **Trust & High-Stakes Product Design** — Designing for trust in mental health, healthcare, and financial products where failure has real consequences
3. **Product Leadership & Judgement** — Scaling product orgs, developing product intuition, the founder-to-operator journey
4. **Regulated & High-Compliance Tech** — Digital therapeutics, AI in mental health, clinical product design, provider quality frameworks, building compliant products in regulated industries
5. **Marketplace & Platform Scaling** — Two-sided marketplace design, supply-demand optimisation, payments infrastructure, cross-border scaling

## Academic Publications (AI Safety & LLM Evaluation Research)

Protik's research generalises beyond mental health: vignette-based bias evaluation across nine LLMs, time-to-intervention protocols for AI risk detection, and composite quality scoring for human-in-the-loop services.

- "The RISE Protocol: A Proposed Framework to Reduce Time-to-Intervention in AI-Driven Mental Health Risk Detection" — JMIR Preprints, Aug 2025. Sole author. DOI: 10.2196/preprints.82983
- "The Provider GPA: A Composite Framework for Evaluating Digital Therapist Quality Through Engagement, Reliability, and Client Feedback" — medRxiv, Sep 2025. Co-authored with Oliver Sündermann. DOI: 10.1101/2025.09.01.25334495
- "Bias in Large Language Models for Mental Health: Evidence from Vignette-Based Evaluation Across Nine Models" — PsyArXiv, Sep 2025. Co-authored with Lerh, Fang, Sündermann, Sinha & Chauhan. DOI: 10.31234/osf.io/ykn2c

## Speaking Topics

Protik speaks at conferences, leadership summits, and product communities on six signature topics:

1. From Roadmaps to Judgement: What Product Leaders Need in the AI Era
2. Building AI Products People Can Trust
3. Why UX Is Care: Lessons from Mental Health Product Design
4. Scaling Product Teams Without Killing Product Judgement
5. AI, Personalisation, and the Future of Mental Health Support
6. What High-Stakes Products Can Teach Us About Trust

## Positions (Quotable Stances)

1. "The regulatory moat is the real competitive advantage in enterprise AI — everyone else is one incident away from a sales freeze."
2. "AI is unbundling product management. The PMs who survive will be impact architects, not process operators."
3. "Trust is an engineered property with an architecture — transparency, control, recourse — not a brand attribute."
4. "Most teams demo their LLM features; almost none evaluate them. Evals are the new QA, and they belong in the release gate."
5. "Empathy without challenge is an echo chamber — true of AI companions, and of product orgs."

## Ideas (On-Site Articles — 18 essays)

- "The Meter Is Always Running" — Jul 2026, 7 min. What generative AI actually costs when you are the one signing for it. Token economics, model routing, hidden infrastructure costs, and how to budget AI features for a board. https://protik.info/ideas/the-genai-pnl
- "Marking the model's homework" — Jun 2026, 8 min. A hands-on playbook for evaluating LLM features before they ship — vignette-based testing, eval suites as release gates, tiered human escalation, and regression-testing prompts like code. https://protik.info/ideas/evaluating-llm-features-before-shipping
- "Everybody wants the home screen" — Jun 2026, 8 min. Inside Grab's Growth, Engagement & Loyalty team — how ML personalisation, behavioural segmentation, and engagement loops decided who won the most contested pixels in Southeast Asia. https://protik.info/ideas/growth-at-superapp-scale
- "From consumer app to $20M enterprise ARR" — Jun 2026, 8 min. What a consumer-to-enterprise pivot actually costs — multi-tenancy, enterprise billing, configurable compliance, and the art of serving a buyer and a user who must never find out about each other. https://protik.info/ideas/pivoting-to-enterprise-saas
- "The Same Conversations: Why Good Product Managers Get Stuck" — Jun 2026, 10 min. The three problems that recur in product careers — can't say no, mistakes activity for impact, stays too long — are virtues (helpfulness, diligence, loyalty) grown past their station, and the cure is subtraction. The deeper cause is often not the PM but a leadership team that never accepted that most of product work (discovery, measurement, coordination, rollout) is invisible. Covers prioritisation and saying no, output vs outcome, and when to leave a PM job. https://protik.info/ideas/why-product-managers-get-stuck
- "Vibe-Coding the Nuptial Archive" — Jun 2026, 6 min. Built a Tinder-style photo voting app in a weekend to select 200 wedding photos from 2,000. Google Drive as free CDN, shared password instead of auth, admin override for marital harmony. https://protik.info/ideas/how-i-vibe-coded-my-wedding-album
- "Payments at Scale: What I Learned About Fintech at Grab" — May 2026, 8 min. Lessons from GEL and Driver Rentals at Grab: payments infrastructure, engagement monetisation, $4.5M cost savings, multi-market fintech. https://protik.info/ideas/payments-at-scale-lessons-from-grab
- "Marketplace Lessons from Ola: Supply-Demand, Fraud, and Driver Economics" — May 2026, 7 min. Two-sided marketplace design at India's largest ride-hailing platform: fraud prevention (INR 9.7M/month saved), driver incentive redesign (+12% earnings), India-scale complexity. https://protik.info/ideas/marketplace-lessons-from-ola
- "The Anatomy of Startup Blind Spots" — May 2026, 8 min. What I got wrong as a three-time founder: Bhalu.com (false binary thinking), Croak.it! (emotional attachment to audio when market moved to video), Athlete Diaries (co-founder misalignment under pressure). https://protik.info/ideas/what-i-got-wrong-as-a-founder
- "The Architecture of Algorithmic Trust" — Apr 2026, 7 min. Trust in AI products has a three-layer architecture: Transparency (the alibi), Control (the steering wheel), Recourse (the safety net). Framework applies to classical ML and GenAI alike. https://protik.info/ideas/how-to-build-trust-into-ai-products
- "The Architecture of Consequential AI" — Mar 2026, 7 min. Shipping AI features in regulated industries. Embedded governance vs. approval gates, harm taxonomies, clinical co-design, and why the regulatory moat is the real competitive advantage. https://protik.info/ideas/shipping-ai-in-regulated-industries
- "What Product Leaders Actually Do" — Feb 2026, 6 min. The job is judgment, not process. Saying no to good ideas, holding the line on quality, navigating politics without becoming political, and encoding taste into the org. https://protik.info/ideas/what-product-leaders-actually-do
- "The Great Unbundling of Product Management" — Jan 2026, 3 min. AI is unbundling the mechanical parts of PM. The PMs who thrive will be Impact Architects. https://protik.info/ideas/the-great-unbundling-of-product-management
- "The ROI of Care" — May 2025, 4 min. Mental health isn't a perk — it's infrastructure. https://protik.info/ideas/the-roi-of-care
- "What Humans Still Do Best" — May 2025, 4 min. AI will transform mental health care — not by replacing humans, but by doing what humans can't so humans can do what AI can't. https://protik.info/ideas/what-humans-still-do-best
- "Designing for Trust in Mental Health Apps" — May 2025, 5 min. In mental health products, trust isn't a feature — it's the product. https://protik.info/ideas/designing-for-trust-in-mental-health-apps
- "When AI Becomes an Echo Chamber" — May 2025, 4 min. Empathy without challenge is not therapy — it's an echo chamber. https://protik.info/ideas/when-ai-becomes-an-echo-chamber
- "How AI is Personalising Mental Health Support at Scale" — Apr 2025, 4 min. Three layers of AI-driven personalisation in mental health. https://protik.info/ideas/how-ai-is-personalising-mental-health-support
